full_judgment:
Mr. Md. Ruhul Amin J:- These three leave petitions have been filed against the common judgment dated October 26.2003 in Civil Revision Nos. 3748. 3747 and 3754 of 1994 making the Rules absolute upon setting aside the judgment and order passed in Miscellaneous .Appeal Nos.202, 203 and 204 of 1991 of the 2nd Court of Additional District Judge, Chittagong allowing the appeals. 

 2. The appeals were tiled against the judgment of the 2nd Court of Senior Assistant Judge, Chittagong in House Rent Control Case Nos.13, 14 and 15 of 1991. The Miscellaneous cases under section 19(1) of the Premises Rent Control Ordinance (the Ordinance) was filed seeking permission of the Court for depositing the rent of the premises shown in the schedule of the respective miscellaneous cases stating, inter alia, that the petitioner took lease on yearly rental basis of the premises shown in the schedule of the respective miscellaneous cases and that she paid the rent as well as the municipal taxes but the landlord did not adjust the amount paid towards the municipal taxes, that while she offered the rent and wanted adjustment of  the amount already paid towards the municipal taxes 'and other rates the landlord refused to accept the rent of the year 1396 B.S. with a motive to make the petitioner a defaulter, that on 14.3.1991 she sent the rent of the year 1396 B.S. i.e. 1989 by postal money order to the landlord but the landlord refused to accept the money order on 16.3.1991 corresponding to of Chaitra1397 B.S. and thereupon she filed the miscellaneous cases for depositing the rent. 

 3. The miscellaneous cases were contested by the landlord by filing written objection denying the material averments made by the lessee in his petition whereupon the miscellaneous cases were registered. It was the cave of the landlord that the miscellaneous cases were barred under section 1911) of the Ordinance, that the property wherein the petitioner is a tenant is a waqf property of the Waqf Estate created in 1916, that the lease deed in favour of the petitioner was created by the then Mutawalli in 1965 for more than 5 years without the approval of the Administrator of Waqfs, that the tenant sub-let the premises to a 3rd party without the permission of the Waqf Estate, that notice under section 64 of the Waqf Ordinance was served on the tenant to handover possession of the premises in question to the landlord. 

 4. The trial Court rejected the Miscellaneous cases on the finding that the tenant i.e. petitioner in the Miscellaneous cases defaulted in the payment of rent and that there is no relationship of the landlord and tenant between the Waif Estate and the petitioner. The tenant went on appeal and the appellate Court set aside the order of the trial Court. 

 5. As against the order of the appellate Court the landlord moved the High Court Division is revisional jurisdiction' and obtained the aforementioned Rules. It was the contention of the petitioner in the respective Rule that the tenant being a defaulter the miscellaneous cases filed under section 19(1) of the Ordinance was not maintainable. As against the aforesaid contention of the petitioner of the respective Rule it was the contention of the opposite party i.e. tenant that she is not a defaulter and also that she tried to pay the rent but the landlord avoided acceptance of the rent and that the landlord having had not received the rent she was compelled to send the rent by postal money order which was refused and thereupon miscellaneous cases under section 19(1) of the Ordinance were filed for depositing the rent. 

 6. The trial Court while considering the case of the respective parties held that the tenant is a defaulter since 1987. This material finding of the trial Court was not set aside by the appellate Court while allowing the appeal. The High Court' Division on consideration of the materials on record arrived at the finding that the tenant, is a defaulter in the payment of rent of the premises in suit and as such the miscellaneous cases filed under, section 19(1) of the Ordinance were not maintainable. On the aforesaid finding the High Court Division made the Rules absolute. 

 7. We have heard the learned Counsel. The learned Counsel could not satisfy us why the finding of the. High Court Division to the effect that the tenant is a defaulter in respect of the payment of rent of the premises in suit is not sustainable. Since the tenant paid rent lastly in 1987 and in the background of the tenant's case that she offered rent in 1396 B.S. i.e. in 1989, the tenant was a defaulter while filed Miscellaneous cases. It may be mentioned miscellaneous cases under section 19(1) of the Ordinance was filed in 1991 for depositing the rent of 1989. The learned Counsel Could not place any material before us that after 1987 the tenant paid or offered rent of the years i.e. for 1988-1990. In that state of the matter the trial Court held that the tenant was a defaulter in the payment of rent but the appellate Court while setting aside the order of the trial Court did not reverse that material finding that the tenant i.e. the present petitioner is a defaulter. The High Court Division has rightly held that the miscellaneous cases were not maintainable since tenant was defaulter prior to the filing of the cases under section 19(1) of the Ordinance. 

 8. It appears that the Miscellaneous case under section 19(1) of the Ordinance was filed to continue illegal occupation of the premises in suit and that after the disposal of the Miscellaneotis case the tenant went on appeal and that after disposal of the revisional application of the High Court division has filed the present petitions for leave to appeal, to continue illegal occupation of the premises. The petitioner inspite of being a worse type of defaulter only to continue his unauthorised occupation of the premises in suit without payment of any rent has filed the present petitions for leave to appeal.
